posts.body:
Recently, for our project, we wanted to implement larger maps that extend beyond what is visible on the screen. The map in question is a school hallway, where we placed a few lockers in the middle. The player can walk behind these lockers, so we created an overlay for the parts they should be able to pass behind.
However, the issue is that the overlay doesn't stay in place as the player moves around the map. Instead, it follows the player, causing the lockers to appear duplicated and making the scene look incorrect.
I attach a video that shows the issue more clearly. Is there a way to fix this with a plug in or a specific parameter?

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Sure, no problem.
I don't know her reason why she doesn't want to use plugins.
But uhm... Here is an important note...
You purely draw it like that, so she can make characters appear behind the object? There are 18452 better ways to do it, She just has to put the top of those cabinets in the tileset, and mark it with a star in the tileset editor.
X means on same level (a.k.a can not pass), O is below your level and * means above your level.
Parallax mapping is for... well... everything you can't do with the tilesets. Like, go off grid, use more than 2 layers and to use large foregrounds, like buildings or trees blocking your view partly.
I mean, you could do it this way, but that is just multiplying the work 100-fold, mostly for you, the artist.
No offense, but I think your friend should follow the tutorials on the basics of RPG maker, because she isn't using it right. This is really the basics of the engine. This should never have been a problem. I don't want to be mean, I just hope she takes my advice, because it will really help, a lot.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
You can go behind them, by default:
The bottom half (the one you didn't put in the parallax) should be marked X, meaning: "Can not pass"
The top half, is higher than your player, so if you mark that a *, you can walk under it/behind it.
I promise, this way you absolutely get the result you try to get.
The rest of the map is just mapping right? Or is everything parallax? Because I do see the top-half scrolling with the map as well. If that is just normal mapping, then it already is in the tile-set already. And marked as passible, maybe even as "above player".
Look... This example is made with the Time Fantasy set I currently use. (Too lazy to start a default projetc for a single screenshot)
The trees I marked a star everywhere, except for the where the tree meets the ground. Here I marked it an X.  And ground floor where I can pass, next to the tree, is marked O
This way, I can walk around the tree, behind and in front of the tree, but not trough the tree.
The engine is designed for your characters to walk behind those.
